title: "2024 Trust Across Institutions"
format: html

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(readxl)
library(usmap)

project_root <- "/Users/BenjaminMarek/Desktop/Hoover_Hartney_Project"
base_path <- file.path(project_root, "MRP", "State Level", "Comprehensive Institutional Trust 2024")

# MRP estimates
mrp_congress <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Congress", "mrp_pooled_congress.rds"))
mrp_media <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Media", "mrp_pooled_media.rds"))
mrp_military <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Military", "mrp_pooled_military.rds"))
mrp_police <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Police", "mrp_pooled_police.rds"))
mrp_religious <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Religious Leaders", "mrp_pooled_religious_leaders.rds"))
mrp_scotus <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "SCOTUS", "mrp_pooled_scotus.rds"))
mrp_universities <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Universities", "mrp_pooled_unis.rds"))
mrp_schools <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Public Schools", "mrp_pooled_pubsch.rds"))

mrp_estimates <- bind_rows(mrp_congress |> mutate(institution = "congress"),
  mrp_media |> mutate(institution = "media"),
  mrp_military |> mutate(institution = "military"),
  mrp_police |> mutate(institution = "police"),
  mrp_religious |> mutate(institution = "religious"),
  mrp_scotus |> mutate(institution = "scotus"),
  mrp_universities |> mutate(institution = "universities"),
  mrp_schools |> mutate(institution = "schools"))

# Fitted models
fit_congress <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Congress", "2024_pooled_congress_mr.rds"))
fit_media <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Media", "2024_pooled_media_mr.rds"))
fit_military <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Military", "2024_pooled_military_mr.rds"))
fit_police <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Police", "2024_pooled_police_mr.rds"))
fit_religious <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Religious Leaders", "2024_pooled_religious_leaders_mr.rds"))
fit_scotus <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "SCOTUS", "2024_pooled_scotus_mr.rds"))
fit_universities <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Universities", "2024_pooled_unis_mr.rds"))
fit_schools <- read_rds(file.path(base_path, "Public Schools", "2024_pooled_pubsch_mr.rds"))

fits <- list(congress = fit_congress,
  media = fit_media,
  military = fit_military,
  police = fit_police,
  religious = fit_religious,
  scotus = fit_scotus,
  universities = fit_universities,
  schools = fit_schools)
```

## Overview
Overall, schools are fairly middle of the row in institutional trust, with a mean of 0.354. However, so far as I can tell from this data, trust in them does appear to function differently. 

As an institution, schools are highly individually highly partisan, with a strong Democratic lean (PID coefficient -1.41) like universities and media. However, it's also weakly predicted by state partisanship (trump_z coefficient close to 0, and the correlation with trump_z is only r = -0.58). Furthermore, schools had the second highest state-level variance unexplained by the model (behind only religious leaders, with religion not being regressed on). 

With regards to demographics, schools had a much flatter age gradient than most other institutions. The other main finding was a large racial category gap, which was significantly larger for public schools than universities.

# Basics
## Summary Stats by Institution
```{r}
#| echo: false

# Summary stat df for all institutions w/ coefficients

summary_stats <- fits |>
  imap_dfr(\(fit, inst) {
    fe <- fixef(fit)
    vc <- VarCorr(fit, summary = TRUE)
    est <- mrp_estimates |> filter(institution == inst) |> pull(p_mrp_est)
    tibble(institution = inst,
      pid_rep = fe["pid3_mrpRepublican", "Estimate"],
      pid_rep_se = fe["pid3_mrpRepublican", "Est.Error"],
      trump_z = fe["trump_z", "Estimate"],
      trump_z_se = fe["trump_z", "Est.Error"],
      sd_state = vc$STATE$sd[, "Estimate"],
      mean_trust = mean(est),
      sd_trust = sd(est),
      min_trust = min(est),
      max_trust = max(est))
  })

summary_stats
```

Military clearly leads in trust (0.629) while media and Congress sit at the bottom at (0.178 and 0.188). Schools and universities have very similar means (0.354 and 0.367).

### State-level Trust Correlations
```{r}
#| echo: false

# Correlations between raw state trust scores
cor_matrix <- mrp_estimates |>
  select(STATE, institution, p_mrp_est) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = institution, values_from = p_mrp_est) |>
  select(-STATE) |>
  cor()

cor_matrix |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "inst1") |>
  pivot_longer(-inst1, names_to = "inst2", values_to = "r") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = inst1, y = inst2, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(r, 2)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue", mid = "white", high = "firebrick", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "r", title = "State-Level Trust Correlations") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Correlations of raw trust numbers across states among institutions.

# PID
### Coefficient Positions
```{r}
#| echo: false

# Individual vs. contextual partisanship coefficients
coef_data <- fits |>
  imap_dfr(\(fit, inst) {
    fe <- fixef(fit)
    tibble(
      institution = inst,
      pid_rep = fe["pid3_mrpRepublican", "Estimate"],
      pid_rep_lower = fe["pid3_mrpRepublican", "Q2.5"],
      pid_rep_upper = fe["pid3_mrpRepublican", "Q97.5"],
      trump_z = fe["trump_z", "Estimate"],
      trump_z_lower = fe["trump_z", "Q2.5"],
      trump_z_upper = fe["trump_z", "Q97.5"]
    )})

ggplot(coef_data, aes(x = pid_rep, y = trump_z, label = institution)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = trump_z_lower, ymax = trump_z_upper), width = 0, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = pid_rep_lower, xmax = pid_rep_upper), height = 0, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_text(vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Individual Partisan Effect (Republican vs Democrat)",
    y = "Contextual Effect (trump_z)",
    title = "Institutional Trust: Individual vs Contextual Partisan Effects"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Controlling for individual partisnaship, trust in schools has essentially zero contextual effect from the percent of the state voting for Trump. Similar for universiteis, media, and Congress, but notably lower than military, religious leaders, and SCOTUS.

### Trust-State Partisanship Correlations
```{r}
#| echo: false

# Correlation between how much a state voted for Trump and trust in institution
state_trump <- read_excel(file.path(project_root, "Data", "Election Results", "2024presgeresults.xlsx")) |>
  filter(complete.cases(STATE)) |>
  transmute(
    STATE = case_match(STATE,
      "AL" ~ "01", "AK" ~ "02", "AZ" ~ "04", "AR" ~ "05", "CA" ~ "06",
      "CO" ~ "08", "CT" ~ "09", "DE" ~ "10", "DC" ~ "11", "FL" ~ "12",
      "GA" ~ "13", "HI" ~ "15", "ID" ~ "16", "IL" ~ "17", "IN" ~ "18",
      "IA" ~ "19", "KS" ~ "20", "KY" ~ "21", "LA" ~ "22", "ME" ~ "23",
      "MD" ~ "24", "MA" ~ "25", "MI" ~ "26", "MN" ~ "27", "MS" ~ "28",
      "MO" ~ "29", "MT" ~ "30", "NE" ~ "31", "NV" ~ "32", "NH" ~ "33",
      "NJ" ~ "34", "NM" ~ "35", "NY" ~ "36", "NC" ~ "37", "ND" ~ "38",
      "OH" ~ "39", "OK" ~ "40", "OR" ~ "41", "PA" ~ "42", "RI" ~ "44",
      "SC" ~ "45", "SD" ~ "46", "TN" ~ "47", "TX" ~ "48", "UT" ~ "49",
      "VT" ~ "50", "VA" ~ "51", "WA" ~ "53", "WV" ~ "54", "WI" ~ "55", "WY" ~ "56"
    ),
    trump_share = TRUMP / (TRUMP + HARRIS))

mrp_estimates |>
  left_join(state_trump, by = "STATE") |>
  group_by(institution) |>
  summarise(r_trump = cor(p_mrp_est, trump_share)) |>
  arrange(r_trump)
```

State-level trust in schools is negatively correlated with how heavily a state voted for trump (-0.582). However, the relationship is far less strong than universities (-0.920) or media (-0.878), or the Republican coded cluster (religious leaders, police, military, SCOTUS).

## Unexplained Variance
```{r}
#| echo: false

# Graph of unexplained state level variation for each institution
fits |>
   imap_dfr(\(fit, inst) {
     vc <- VarCorr(fit, summary = TRUE)
     tibble(
       institution = inst,
       sd_state = vc$STATE$sd[, "Estimate"],
       sd_state_lower = vc$STATE$sd[, "Q2.5"],
       sd_state_upper = vc$STATE$sd[, "Q97.5"]
     )}) |>
   ggplot(aes(x = reorder(institution, sd_state), y = sd_state)) +
   geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = sd_state_lower, ymax = sd_state_upper)) +
   coord_flip() +
   labs(x = NULL, y = "Residual State SD", 
    title = "Unexplained State-Level Variation by Institution") + theme_minimal()
```

Schools have notably higher variation unexplained model at the state-level than other institutions (second only to religious leaders). Most institutions clustered between 0.06 and 0.1 residual state SD. Only religious leaders higher than schools (perhaps because not MRPing on religion). Partisanship explains most geographic variation for universities/media but not for schools.

### Posterior Draws
```{r}
# Pulls posterior draws from independent models (grain of salt) for variance and trump_z and compares them
post_sd_schools <- as_draws_df(fit_schools)$sd_STATE__Intercept
post_sd_unis <- as_draws_df(fit_universities)$sd_STATE__Intercept
post_trump_schools <- as_draws_df(fit_schools)$b_trump_z
post_trump_unis <- as_draws_df(fit_universities)$b_trump_z

mean(post_sd_schools > post_sd_unis)
mean(post_trump_schools > post_trump_unis)
```

Comparing posterior distributions from separate models: in 98% of paired draws, school sd_state exceeds university. Models fit independently so not definitive but degree of distance means overlap unlikely.


### Unexplained Variance-State Partisanship Relationship
```{r}
#| echo: false

# Correlation between unexplained variance and state partisanship
school_blups <- ranef(fit_schools)$STATE |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "STATE") |>
  select(STATE, blup = Estimate.Intercept) |>
  left_join(state_trump, by = "STATE")

cor(school_blups$blup, school_blups$trump_share)

# Graph of value of residuals compared to state trump vote share
school_blups |>
  ggplot(aes(x = trump_share, y = blup)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Trump Vote Share (2024)",
    y = "School Trust Residual (BLUP)",
    title = "School Trust Residuals vs State Partisanship"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

School unexplained variance is uncorrelated with state partisanship. Seems to be genuinely unexplained by the model, not residual partisan/demographic signals.

### High Residual/Outlier States

```{r}
#| echo: false

# Prints states with highest unexplained variance
ranef(fit_schools)$STATE |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "fips") |>
  left_join(fips_info(), by = "fips") |>
  arrange(desc(abs(Estimate.Intercept))) |>
  select(full, Estimate.Intercept, Est.Error.Intercept)
```

These states have the most extreme variation from the value predicted by the model (either positive or negative). Negative: Nevada (-0.302), Lousiana (-0.267). Positive: South Dakota (0.238), Nebraska (0.224), Utah (0.221). Possibly correlated with actual school performance metrics?




# Demographics Effects
## Education Random Effects 
```{r}
#| echo: false

# Comparison of educ random effects by inst
educ_effects <- fits |>
  imap_dfr(\(fit, inst) {
    ranef(fit)$educ_mrp |>
      as_tibble(rownames = "educ") |>
      transmute(institution = inst, educ, effect = Estimate.Intercept)}) |>
  mutate(educ = factor(educ, levels = c("HS or less", "Some college", "College grad", "Postgrad")))

educ_effects |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = institution, values_from = effect) |>
  arrange(educ)
```

## Race Random Effects
```{r}
#| echo: false

# Comparison of race random effects by inst
race_effects <- fits |>
  imap_dfr(\(fit, inst) {
    ranef(fit)$race_mrp |>
      as_tibble(rownames = "race") |>
      transmute(institution = inst, race, effect = Estimate.Intercept)})

race_effects |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = institution, values_from = effect)
```

```{r}
# Pulls race posterior draws for schoosl and universities and compares them. Independent models, so grain of salt
post_schools_white <- as_draws_df(fit_schools)$`r_race_mrp[White,Intercept]`
post_schools_black <- as_draws_df(fit_schools)$`r_race_mrp[Black,Intercept]`
post_unis_white <- as_draws_df(fit_universities)$`r_race_mrp[White,Intercept]`
post_unis_black <- as_draws_df(fit_universities)$`r_race_mrp[Black,Intercept]`

gap_schools <- post_schools_white - post_schools_black
gap_unis <- post_unis_white - post_unis_black

mean(gap_schools > gap_unis)
```

## Range of Log Odds Across Demographic Categories
```{r}
#| echo: false

# Comparison of gap in log odds of random effects by inst
demographic_ranges <- fits |>
  imap_dfr(\(fit, inst) {
    educ_vals <- ranef(fit)$educ_mrp |> as_tibble() |> pull(Estimate.Intercept)
    race_vals <- ranef(fit)$race_mrp |> as_tibble() |> pull(Estimate.Intercept)
    age_vals <- ranef(fit)$age_mrp |> as_tibble() |> pull(Estimate.Intercept)
    tibble(
      institution = inst, 
      educ_range = diff(range(educ_vals)),
      race_range = diff(range(race_vals)),
      age_range = diff(range(age_vals))
    )}) |>
  arrange(desc(educ_range))
```

```{r}
demographic_ranges
```

Schools have less wide gap in trust across educational categories than universities, but significant and more than any other institution. Schools seem to be significantly more racially stratified than universities (supported moderately by comparison of posterior draws from independent models), but seem to be less than police, religious leaders, and Congress. Schools have notably smaller range across age categories than any other institution.

### Limitation
Parental status not included (though interestingly age range is flat). Also no deep MRP interaction for (pid3:trump_z), though given the lack of contextual effects shouldn't matter too much.

## Model Run
```{r}
formula <- trust_binary ~  sex_mrp + (1|pid3_mrp) + 
  (1|age_mrp) + (1|educ_mrp) + (1|race_mrp) + (1|STATE) + (1|STATE:educ_mrp) + (1|STATE:race_mrp) + (1|STATE:pid3_mrp) + + (1|pid3_mrp:trump_z) + trump_z
```
